content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each type
Give examples of organisms that reproduce sexually and asexually
Explain the importance of genetic variation
is a fundamental characteristic of life - the process by which organisms produce offspring. There are two main types:
(involving one parent). Each has advantages and disadvantages.
Reproduction involving one parent, producing offspring genetically identical to the parent
Reproduction involving two parents, where gametes fuse to form a new individual
May not cope if conditions change
Asexual when conditions are good (fast reproduction), sexual when conditions change (variation for survival)
Asexual reproduction only occurs in simple organisms
Many complex plants use asexual reproduction
Sexual reproduction always requires two different individuals
Asexual reproduction is primitive and inferior
It's highly successful in stable environments
Asexual: one parent, no gametes, produces clones
Sexual: two parents, gametes fuse, produces variation
Asexual is fast and energy-efficient but no variation
Sexual produces variation but is slower and needs mate
Genetic variation is essential for adaptation and survival
Some organisms use both depending on conditions
Sexual reproduction drives evolution through variation
